description: [QUARANTINED -- NOT RUNNABLE END-TO-END BY THE SCRIPT RUNNER. Do not read a failure of this script as an app defect.] This script is EXCLUDED from the default sweep (run-winwright-tests.ps1 $excludedFromSweep) because the WinWright script runner SKIPS ww_wait and REJECTS ww_assert, so there is no way to express a settle between a Flutter dialog animating in and the next selector query. Symptom when run anyway via -TestName f56: a step returns success, then the NEXT selector resolves 0 elements (e.g. 'Save'/'Enter TLD' pre-settle). Verified again 2026-07-31. Every SELECTOR below is individually verified live and correct -- the gap is runner settle, not the selectors and not the app. Reliable execution of this lifecycle belongs in integration_test (F99), which has pumpAndSettle. F56 create+delete block rule lifecycle (Sprint 41 F97, round 2 fix 2026-06-14). Creates a Top-Level-Domain block rule for TLD 'museum' (IANA-registered, verified absent from dev DB at authoring time), confirms the save dialog, then uses the Manage Rules search box to locate and delete the created rule in a teardown testCase -- net DB change is zero. TEST DATA: 'museum' chosen because 'xyz' (prior candidate) was already in the dev DB as source_domain='*.xyz'. 'museum' is in kIanaTlds (iana_tlds.dart) and had count=0 in the top_level_domain rules at time of authoring. Generated pattern: @.*\.museum$ , source_domain: *.museum. FIX 1 -- RADIO SELECTOR (CORRECTED Sprint 52, F131): the Sprint 41 text here claimed the RadioButton could not be selected and that the fix was to click the PARENT GROUP (type=Group[name*='Top-Level Domain']). That is WRONG and it is what misled Sprint 51 into concluding 'the create path is not drivable'. Clicking a Group hits a container with no selection behavior. The correct target is the RADIOBUTTON ITSELF with useInvokePattern:false -- verified live 2026-07-31 (input name flips to 'Enter TLD (...)', confirm dialog reads 'Type: Top-Level Domain / Source: *.museum'). ww_invoke correctly FAILS on it ('does not support InvokePattern') because radios use SelectionItemPattern, not InvokePattern -- proper UIA behavior, not a defect. The app was never broken; the selector was. FIX 2 -- INPUT FIELD NAME IS MODE-DEPENDENT: in Top-Level-Domain mode the input is type=Edit[name*='Enter TLD'] (full name 'Enter TLD (e.g., .cc, .xyz, .store)'). In Entire-Domain mode (default) the input is type=Edit[name='Enter email, domain, or URL']. The prior script used the Entire-Domain field name in TLD mode, so input was silently ignored. FIX 3 -- SAVE BUTTON OFF-SCREEN + INVOKE->CLICK: ww_window_state maximize added as first step. Verified live: after maximize, Save Rule is IsOffscreen=False at y=734 (window 1020px+ tall), so no ww_scroll step is needed. ww_click (not ww_invoke) used for Save Rule. SCROLL FALLBACK: ww_scroll mode=into_view was initially included but caused a race condition -- the scroll repositioned the Flutter scroll container just before ww_click Save Rule, and the confirm dialog did not appear. Removed. Maximize alone is sufficient on this machine (1920x1080). CONFIRMATION DIALOG: 'Confirm Block Rule' Alert with Button[name='Save'] -- verified live via ww_dump_tree immediately after Save Rule click. TEARDOWN: search '*.museum', click Button[name*='View rule details'], Delete x2 (first Delete opens 'Delete Rule' confirm, second confirms), Back x2 to home -- all selectors verified live.

testCases.title: Create TLD block rule for museum

steps._comment: PRIMING QUERY: Flutter builds its UIA semantics tree lazily IN RESPONSE TO A QUERY, not on a timer -- on a cold-launched app the first query returns an opaque FLUTTERVIEW pane. This also maximizes, so nothing is off-screen (Save Rule sits below the fold otherwise).

F135 (Sprint 52) changed the desktop DEFAULT screen to Review No Rule Items when at least one account exists, and Settings now resolves its account lazily -- so the account-picker step this script used to have is GONE. Settings opens straight onto the General tab.
PROOF OF ARRIVAL: the General tab exists only once Settings is open. Tabs project as Text nodes, so they need the physical-mouse path.

Sprint 52 F131 CORRECTION -- the Sprint 51 claim that the Rule Type radios 'do not select' was WRONG, and the reason matters. Sprint 51 targeted the PARENT GROUP (`type=Group[name*='Top-Level Domain']`), following a Sprint 41 note. Clicking a Group hits a container with no selection behavior, so nothing happened -- and the conclusion drawn was 'radios cannot be selected'. Targeting the RADIOBUTTON ITSELF with useInvokePattern:false works, verified live 2026-07-31: the input's name flips from 'Enter email, domain, or URL' to 'Enter TLD (...)' and the confirm dialog reads 'Type: Top-Level Domain / Source: *.museum'. Note ww_invoke correctly FAILS here ('does not support InvokePattern') because radios use SelectionItemPattern -- proper UIA behavior, not a defect. The app was never broken; the selector was.
PROOF OF EFFECT: this Edit is named 'Enter TLD (...)' ONLY in TLD mode. If the radio had not selected, the field would still be 'Enter email, domain, or URL' and this step would resolve 0 elements.
Save Rule sits below the fold on a non-maximized window; ww_invoke would report success WITHOUT pressing it, so the mouse path is used deliberately.
PROOF OF EFFECT: the 'Confirm Block Rule' dialog appears only if Save Rule actually fired.
